title: Define LTS interop contracts and exception matrix across runtime / API / SDK / Console
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Create a single canonical LTS interoperability contract and an ‘exceptions matrix’ that explicitly records which combinations of runtime, Redwood API, official SDKs, and Console features are supported, best-effort, or unsupported for each LTS channel. This ticket captures scoping, policy decisions, rollout-gates, and the artifacts needed to publish the matrix and automate compatibility checks in CI and the console UI.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable LTS interop matrix (CSV and JSON) covering runtime, API surface version, SDK minor versions, and console feature flags exists and is checked into //release-engineering/lts-matrix
Definitions for supported | best-effort | unsupported are documented and approved by Platform and SDK leads
Rollout gates for upgrades are codified (health checks, evaluation prompt sets, latency regressions, telemetry thresholds) and integrated into the canary pipeline
Console shows LTS compatibility status per customer (based on pinned model/runtime/API/SDK) and surfaces upgrade recommendations
CI job fails merge if a PR introduces an unexpected breaking surface for an LTS channel unless an exception is filed and approved
plan: Draft domain model for matrix columns and status semantics (runtime binary, runtime API, API spec version, public SDKs, console feature flags)
Work with SDK leads to pin supported minor semver ranges and define minimum API contract for each LTS channel
Define rollout-gates and measurable thresholds with Observability (latency p99, token cost delta, error-rate change, eval quality regression)
Prototype a CSV/JSON schema and a small Python tool to validate compatibility predicates
Integrate matrix checks into the release CI and the console compatibility UI
Run a pilot for runtime-1.22 LTS across a subset of internal customers and capture telemetry
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with Release Eng, SDK, Console, and Observability — agreed on top-level goals and timeline
2026-03-11: Drafted initial column set and semantics; shared with runtime and SDK owners for feedback
2026-03-12: Observability proposed p99 latency + 5% and token-cost +3% as soft-fail thresholds for canary; pending confirmation from product
2026-03-12: Created prototype JSON schema for matrix and a simple validator script (branch: release/lts-matrix-proto)
risks: Matrix divergence: owners fail to keep matrix up to date causing stale guidance
Overly strict gates block necessary runtime patches during emergencies
Edge-case combos (older SDK + newer runtime) create noisy exception filings
Console UI complexity: exposing too many states confuses customers leading to support load
notes: We should treat exceptions as first-class artifacts with expire dates and required approvers
Consider storing matrix in a single source of truth repo and exposing via a small service to avoid drift
Plan to run two weeks of shadow checks against production traffic before enforcing CI failures
